info.title: MadeOnSol API
info.description:
Real-time Solana & Robinhood Chain trading intelligence — KOL wallet trades, deployer reputation, token buyer-quality scoring, wallet tracking, and copy-trade signals across both chains (Robinhood Chain paths under `/rhc/*`).

**Data freshness per tier**: live-feed endpoints (KOL feeds, deployer alerts, graduations, first-touches, coordination) are **real-time on PRO and up and on x402 pay-per-call; delayed 5 minutes on the free tier** (delayed responses carry `delay`, `as_of` and an `X-Data-Delay` header). Scores, leaderboards, wallet PnL, holder data and search are real-time on every tier.

**Authentication**: pass `Authorization: Bearer msk_xxx` on every request. See pricing + start free at https://madeonsol.com/pricing (200 calls/day free tier, no payment to start).

**Tiers**: BASIC (free, 200/day) · PRO (€43/mo ≈ $49, 10,000/day) · ULTRA (€131/mo ≈ $149, 100,000/day) · BUSINESS (€400/mo ≈ $456, 500,000/day, embed license + bulk Parquet exports) · ENTERPRISE (custom — SLA, dedicated limits, redistribution; info@madeonsol.com). Pay by card, USDC, or SOL. Full plan comparison: https://madeonsol.com/pricing

**Tier per operation**: every operation carries `x-madeonsol-tier` — the minimum plan that unlocks it, one of `FREE` `PRO` `ULTRA` `BUSINESS` `ENTERPRISE`, read from the route's own gate (a higher plan always passes). The top-level `x-madeonsol-tiers` legend lists each tier's name, price and quota. A call below the gate returns 403 with an `upgrade` block.

**Try it now**: a public demo key works on `/kol/feed`, `/deployer-hunter/alerts`, and `/alpha/leaderboard` — see https://madeonsol.com/api-docs

**Response headers**: every response carries `X-Request-Id` (quote it in support requests). Once your key is authenticated, responses also carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Used` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix epoch seconds); authentication-stage errors (401, invalid-key 403) do not. Quota 429s, concurrency 429s and 503s carry `Retry-After` (seconds). Each operation documents these headers and its error bodies through the reusable `components.headers` and `components.responses`. Free-tier responses past ~70% of the daily quota also carry an `X-MadeOnSol-Quota-Warning` header with an upgrade link.

**Changelog**: see https://madeonsol.com/changelog for recent updates.

RhcHolderGrowthWindow.description: One holder-growth window on /rhc/tokens/{address}/holders. Pools and burn addresses are excluded from every count.

cutoff_block.description: Lowest block observed at-or-after now()−window (resolved from our trade ingest, ~10 blocks/s).

entered.description: Addresses whose first Transfer of this token landed at-or-after cutoff_block (any current balance).

exited.description: Pre-existing holders whose last Transfer in the window left them at zero.

net.description: entered_still_holding − exited ≈ change in holder_count over the window.

RhcTokenRiskSummary.description:
Precomputed risk summary for a Robinhood Chain token, from the same engine as `/rhc/tokens/{address}/risk` (proxy resolution, capability scan, and a live router sell-simulation).

**`null` means NOT ASSESSED, not safe.** The sweep covers tokens with liquidity on a ~24h rotation, so a brand-new or illiquid token has no row yet.

These values are a SNAPSHOT — always read `checked_at`. Sellability can change the moment an owner flips a setting, which is why `/rhc/tokens/{address}/risk` is computed live and never served from this cache. Use this to triage a feed; use the live endpoint before acting on a single token.

sellable.description: `no` means a sell was simulated through the router and REVERTED — bought-but-cannot-sell.

upgradeable.description: Token is a proxy whose implementation can be swapped (EIP-1967 / beacon / legacy). EIP-1167 minimal proxies are NOT upgradeable — the target is baked into immutable code.

score.description: 0–100, conservative. Absence of evidence is not evidence of safety.

wallet_count.description: Number of same-slot bundle wallets (is_bundle: ≥3 buying in one slot)

bundle_kind.description: atomic_tx = ≥3 wallets share one buy tx (definitively atomic); same_slot = the ≥3-same-slot heuristic (possible coincidence); none = no cohort

held_pct_of_supply.description: HEADLINE. Cohort net held ÷ circulating supply, 0–1 (clamped). null when supply is unknown

held_ratio.description: Cohort net held ÷ buy_volume, 0–1. Churn-sensitive — secondary to held_pct_of_supply

buy_volume.description: Cumulative buy-side token volume — NOT distinct tokens; can exceed supply on round-tripping

tokens_held.description: Swap-derived net position (Σbuys−Σsells) — a proxy for on-chain balance, not a holder census

wallets.description: BASIC: empty. PRO: top-10, flags only. ULTRA: full cohort + identity fields.

atomic.description: This wallet is part of an atomic single-tx bundle

Error.description: Generic error envelope. `error` is always present (SDKs match on it). Errors returned after authentication also carry `_rid` and, on paid tiers, `support`; authentication-stage errors (missing/invalid key, origin) carry neither.

error.description: Error message or machine code (e.g. `tier_required`, `rate_limit_exceeded`). Never changed once shipped.

message.description: Human-readable explanation, when `error` is a machine code.

retry_after_seconds.description: When present on a 429/503, the same value is sent as the `Retry-After` header.

signup_url.description: On the missing-key / bad-format 401: where to get a free key.

support.description: Paid tiers, errors after authentication: priority support contact.

_rid.description: Request ID — include when reporting issues

TierRequiredError.description: 403 when the key's tier is below the endpoint's (or a parameter's) gate. `required_tier` matches the operation's `x-madeonsol-tier` or `x-madeonsol-feature-tiers`. ENTERPRISE gates return `contact` instead of `upgrade`.

upgrade.description: The plan that lifts this limit, with price and a checkout link.

reactivate.description: Present (true) when the key's paid subscription has just lapsed and `tier` is the plan it held.

DemoKeyNotAllowedError.description: 403 for the public demo key (`msk_demo_…`) outside its three-endpoint allow-list. `endpoint_tier` is the endpoint's real minimum plan (null when unknown).

upgrade_url.description: Only when the endpoint's tier can be bought at /checkout.

RateLimitError.description: 429 when a quota is exhausted: the daily quota, the per-minute burst, or a free-tier network/key-rotation cap. `datasets` is added on `daily` only.

upgrade.description: The plan that lifts this limit, with price and a checkout link.

reactivate.description: Present (true) when the key's paid subscription has just lapsed and `tier` is the plan it held.

ConcurrencyLimitError.description: 429 from the heavy-query limiter: too many heavy requests in flight for this key (`concurrency`) or for the whole server (`capacity`). Clears as soon as in-flight requests finish.

ServiceUnavailableError.description: 503: a temporary capacity or maintenance condition (e.g. a Postgres statement timeout during a partition move, or the API-key lookup itself being unavailable). Retry after `Retry-After` seconds.

code.description: Machine-readable code where one exists, e.g. `auth_backend_unavailable`.

RhcCopytradeTrackedWallets.description: DEPRECATED 2026-10-04 (kept, still filled): subset of source_wallets in the tracked KOL set (kol_evm_wallets, the set behind /rhc/kol/wallets). KOL enrichment only once source_admission is any_wallet; under the legacy kol_only engine only these can produce a signal. null when the reference read failed.

RhcCopytradeUntrackedWallets.description: DEPRECATED 2026-10-04 (kept, still filled): subset of source_wallets NOT in the tracked KOL set. Under source_admission any_wallet they fire like any other wallet; under the legacy kol_only engine they never produce a signal. null when the reference read failed.

RhcCopytradeOperationalState.description: Whether the rule can fire at all, separate from is_active (the customer switch). Under source_admission any_wallet (2026-10-04) every valid source wallet is followed, KOL or not: eligible; monitoring_pending = the rule changed after the engine's last rule load (live within seconds); monitoring_unavailable = the engine or the trade stream is not reporting, and it fires nothing until it is (see monitoring_reasons); source_capacity_unavailable = the engine's source-wallet cap is reached. Legacy (source_admission kol_only or absent): no_tracked_sources = none of source_wallets is a tracked KOL wallet (kol_evm_wallets on Robinhood Chain, active kol_wallets on Solana), so the rule cannot fire; unknown = the tracking read failed.

RhcCopytradeSourceAdmission.description: Which trades the RUNNING copy-trade engine admits (shared by the Solana and Robinhood Chain rules). any_wallet: a qualifying trade by any source wallet, KOL or not (Robinhood Chain: the ERC-4337 userOp sender on bundled transactions; Solana: the same effective-trader rule as KOL attribution). kol_only: only tracked KOL wallets (kol_evm_wallets / active kol_wallets), legacy. Absent when the engine state could not be read (legacy semantics). Added 2026-10-04.

RhcCopytradeMonitoringReasons.description: Present only with operational_state monitoring_unavailable: the infrastructure reasons (e.g. dex_stream_stale, trade_stream_stale, source_producer_stale, map_stale, bus_disconnected, engine_state_stale). Added 2026-10-04.

RhcCopytradeRuleWarnings.description: Present only when something needs attention (the key is omitted otherwise, never null). Additive — status codes and existing fields never change. Emitted only under source_admission kol_only (legacy); under any_wallet an untracked wallet is not a problem and no warning is attached.

CopytradeSubscription.description: A copy-trade rule: source wallets to mirror, sizing, delivery, and optional MC bounds.

source_wallets.description: Wallets being copied. Any valid Solana wallet once source_admission is any_wallet; under the legacy kol_only engine only active tracked KOL wallets fire — see source_admission and operational_state.

min_trade_sol.description: Skip source trades below this SOL size

sizing_amount.description: fixed = SOL amount, proportional = multiplier (0.5 = half size), percent_source = 0..1

source_wallets_tracked.description: DEPRECATED 2026-10-04 (kept, still filled): subset of source_wallets that are active tracked Solana KOL wallets (the set behind /kol/wallets). KOL enrichment only once source_admission is any_wallet; under the legacy kol_only engine only these produce signals. null when the lookup failed. Added 2026-09-25.

source_wallets_untracked.description: DEPRECATED 2026-10-04 (kept, still filled): subset of source_wallets that are not tracked KOL wallets. Under source_admission any_wallet they fire like any other wallet (no Wallet Tracker entry needed, no Wallet Tracker quota used); under the legacy kol_only engine they never produce a signal. null when the lookup failed. Added 2026-09-25.

WebhookFilters.description: Optional per-event delivery filters on a webhook. wallet_tracker:event (since 2026-09-25): only min_sol, action and conditions on its own fields apply, after the subscriber check; on a webhook subscribed to wallet_tracker:event alone any other named filter is a 400.

action.description: kol:trade, wallet_tracker:event (transfers have no action and are excluded)

types.description: dev:activity only: event types to deliver

deployers.description: dev:activity only: matches deployer_wallet or actor_wallet

conditions.description: ULTRA+ (2026-09-08). Custom { field, op, value } triples ANDed together and evaluated against the raw event payload, on top of the named filters. `field` must be a documented payload field of one of the webhook's subscribed event types (one level of dot-path allowed, e.g. `triggering_trade.sol_amount`); anything else is a 400. Number fields take eq/neq/gt/gte/lt/lte/in, strings eq/neq/in/contains, booleans eq/neq. On PRO the request is a 403 tier_required.

value.description: number | string | boolean, or a non-empty array (≤20) for `in`.

events.description: dev:activity (live since 2026-10-05): developer dev_sell / dev_buy / dev_token_transfer_out / dev_token_transfer_in, projected per tier at delivery (PRO: the developer's own events, raw facts, no identity keys; ULTRA+: identity fields and linked-wallet events from proven links only). Dedupe on data.id. Transfers are partial (most recently active developer wallets only).

TradeCoverage.description: Coverage disclosure for endpoints backed by our persisted trade capture (`token_trades` / early-buyer data). Capture starts 2026-04-12 and persistence is gated to the launchpad pipeline (pump.fun, LaunchLab/bonk, bags) — it is NOT a full Solana trade history. Three separate answers (2026-09-21): `data_observed`/`in_scope` = at least one persisted row (presence, not completeness — a brand-new in-scope mint with no trades yet also reads false), `eligibility` = whether the CURRENT gate admits the subject, `completeness` = always `not_verified`. When no rows exist, zero/empty values mean 'not captured' (see eligibility for why), never 'no activity'.

history_start.description: Epoch seconds of the first persisted trade (2026-04-12).

in_scope.description: Kept for compatibility — same value as data_observed: true = we hold ≥1 persisted trade for this subject · false = none persisted (see eligibility for why — a brand-new in-scope mint also reads false) · null = probe unavailable

eligibility.description: Resolved against the EFFECTIVE production capture settings (refreshed every few minutes; if they cannot be confirmed the answer narrows, never widens). eligible = admitted by the current gate · lapsed = launched via our pipeline, capture window closed under the current settings · excluded = blacklisted · unknown = no evidence the gate admits it (most likely outside the launchpad pipeline; basis capture_state_unavailable = settings could not be confirmed, no claim either way) · admitted_previously = persisted rows prove past admission, current status not established · not_applicable = wallet subjects · null = lookup failed

eligibility_basis.description: Evidence behind eligibility (e.g. unresolved_launch, recently_bonded, revived_curve, pipeline_known, launchlab_pool, bags_vanity_mint, launchpad_proven, resolved_launch, bonded_over_7d, revival_expired, blacklisted, persisted_rows, capture_state_unavailable, lookup_failed)

size_floor.description: Persistence size floor of the same write path (added 2026-09-30). Buys under 0.05 SOL (under $3.50 when paid in USDC/USDT) are not stored; sells that receive SOL are kept at any size. Live streams, prices and candles are not subject to it.

applies_to.example: buys and SOL-spending legs; SOL-receiving sells of any size are kept

note.description: How to read the values (always present since 2026-09-21: eligibility-specific when no rows exist, a completeness caveat when they do).

LaunchCoverage.description: Dataset-scope disclosure injected on every 200 from the launch-pipeline feeds (`/deployer-hunter/*`, `/sniper/*`, `/alpha/*`, `/tokens/almost-bonded`, `/tokens/batch/risk`, `/wallet/batch/classify`) unless the route already carries a more precise per-subject `coverage`. Static: these datasets are built from launchpad ingest (in practice ~99% pump.fun), so an absent wallet/token, an empty profile or a `false` reputation flag means 'not observed by this pipeline', never 'clean' or 'no activity'.

scope.example: launchpad pipeline (pump.fun and LaunchLab/bonk deploys; bags.fm tokens are covered in trade data but their deploys are not attributed here; no direct-to-DEX launches)

note.description: How to read absences and zeros in this response.

market_cap_usd_at_trade.description: Token market cap in USD at the moment of trade (real-time, from our in-memory price tracker — not the post-hoc Dexscreener spot)

price_usd_at_trade.description: Token price in USD at the moment of trade

launchpad.description: Launchpad of origin (`pumpfun` / `launchlab` / `bags`); null for non-launchpad mints.

token_age_minutes.description: Minutes between the token's first observed trade and now (not at trade time); null when the mint has no first-seen record.

kol_strategy_tag.description: Manual strategy tag from the roster, falling back to the auto-classified tag.

kol_auto_strategy_tag.description: Auto-classified trader style — the value `strategy=` filters on.

kol_early_entry_pct_30d.description: Share of the KOL's 30-day buys that were early entries.

kol_is_heating_up.description: KOL's recent performance is trending up vs their own baseline.

kol_percentile_pnl_7d.description: KOL's 7-day PnL percentile across the roster (0-100).

kol_percentile_winrate_7d.description: KOL's 7-day win-rate percentile across the roster (0-100).

deployer.description: Present only when the token has a tracked deployer.

deployer_tier.description: Shortcut for `deployer.tier`; present only when `deployer` is.

token.description: Present only with `include=token` — the `/token/{mint}` snapshot for this row (null past the 20-distinct-mint cap).

median_hold_minutes_30d.description: Median hold time in minutes over the last 30 days.

percentile_early_entry_30d.description: Percentile rank for early entry timing over the last 30 days.

avg_winrate_7d.description: Mean 7d winrate across the cluster's KOLs

entry_rank_avg.description: Avg early-entry percentile (lower = earlier in the trade)

unique_strategies.description: Count of distinct auto_strategy_tag values across the KOLs

time_to_consensus_sec.description: Seconds between first and last KOL buy (full-period span)

peak_window_start.description: Start of densest buy cluster (default 15-min window)

peak_kols.description: Distinct KOLs buying inside the peak window

peak_buys.description: Total buys inside the peak window

exited_count.description: KOLs in the cluster whose sell_sol > buy_sol (net-flow-negative)

coordination_score.description: Composite 0-100 signal score. Weighting exposed via top-level score_version.

market_cap_usd_at_first_buy.description: Market cap (USD) stamped on the cluster's chronologically-first KOL buy. Distinguishes coordinated accumulation at micro-cap from late-stage chasing.

market_cap_usd.description: Current market cap (USD) of the token, sourced from token_prices. Compare against market_cap_usd_at_first_buy for the cluster's MC delta.

mc_change_pct.description: Market-cap % change over each window (e.g. 12.4 = +12.4%). Sparse — only windows with enough mc-tracker history are present. Use to tell whether the cluster is firing into a moving token or before the move.

volume_usd.description: Organic (non-MEV) USD volume over each window. Sparse — same gating as mc_change_pct.

mev_volume_pct.description: MEV-share of total volume over each window (0-100). High value = bot-heavy / sandwich-heavy flow.

history_age_seconds.description: Seconds of mc-tracker history available for this token (capped at 4h05m). Tells you which windows can be trusted. Null when token is untracked.

kols.description: BASIC: array of KOL names (first 3). PRO+: objects {name, wallet, buy_sol, sell_sol, exited} — full wallet addresses on every tier that can call the endpoint (BASIC gets 403 on /kol/coordination).

CoordinationAlertRule.description: A saved /kol/coordination/alerts rule. `created_at` is present on list/GET-one responses; `updated_at` is present on GET-one/PATCH responses (list omits it).

FirstTouchSubscription.description: A saved /kol/first-touches/subscriptions subscription. `created_at` is present on list/GET-one/PATCH responses; `updated_at` is present on GET-one/PATCH responses (list omits it).

confidence.description: Confidence in the PREDICTIVE inputs: counts only buyers whose win rate fed the score (≥3 tokens of history, not bot-flagged, not zero-cost-dump dominated). insufficient_data = none did — the score is the neutral-50 default plus penalties. 1 → low, 5+ → medium, 11+ → high.

avg_historical_win_rate.description: null when no buyer's win rate qualified (confidence insufficient_data)

wallets_with_history.description: Buyers with ≥3 tokens of history (cohort identification — not predictive)

qualified_win_rate_wallets.description: Buyers whose win rate fed the score — the basis of confidence

dump_cluster_count.description: First-20 buyers on the rolling dump-cluster list (wallets whose 5+ recent first-20 appearances are exclusively on tokens that peaked <15 min after deploy; trailing 42d, refreshed daily). Out-of-sample: 3+ such wallets predicted a sub-15-min peak 94% of the time vs 61% base. Informational — does not move the score.

recycled_early_buyer_count.description: First-20 buyers with 5+ recent first-20 cohort appearances of any kind. The count alone predicts nothing; a heavily recycled cohort with dump_cluster_count 0 historically leans runner.

note.description: Present only when no early-buyer data exists for the mint — the score is then a neutral 50 placeholder ("Insufficient buyer data"); check coverage to tell 'no early buyers captured' from 'mint outside the write-gate'.

signal_stats.description: Present only when breakdown.dump_cluster_count ≥ 1 and the daily signal-performance snapshot has a bucket for it. The live, out-of-sample efficacy of that value, so the raw count is readable.

bucket.description: Most specific cumulative-threshold bucket the value qualifies for.

outcome.description: Outcome the hit rate is measured against.

as_of.description: Snapshot time of the signal_performance row.

summary.example: dump_cluster_count=3 (k>=3): 95% of such tokens dumped vs 75% base (1.27× lift), n=349, 14d OOS

wallets_with_history.description: Buyers with ≥3 tokens of history (cohort identification — not predictive)

qualified_win_rate_wallets.description: Buyers whose win rate fed the score — the basis of confidence

Out-of-sample: 3+ such wallets predicted a sub-15-min peak 94% of the time vs 61% base. Informational — does not move the score.

WalletTrackerSummary.description: Per-wallet activity for your Solana tracked wallets over `period` (newest-added first). An empty tracker returns `{ wallets: [], period }` without `interval`.

interval.description: Postgres interval for the period, e.g. "7 days".

coverage_note.description: Fixed disclosure: is_sniper/is_bundler/is_dumper derive from the launchpad trade pipeline — false means 'not observed in covered trades', not 'verified clean'.

is_sniper.description: >=5 tokens early-bought & >=80% flipped <5min (behavior-updated hourly). Pump.fun-pipeline scoped; false = not observed, not verified clean

is_bundler.description: Bought >1 token in the same block, ever (lifetime flag)

is_dumper.description: >=5 dump cohorts + 0 runner cohorts in rolling 42d window (recomputed daily)

dump_cluster.description: Raw dump-cluster cohort counts (present when the wallet has >=5 recent early-buyer cohort appearances)

top_tokens.description: Top traded tokens (90d window) with realized PnL. Cross-joined with deployer-tokens for symbol + peak MC where available.

trading_style.description: Behavioural signals: avg trade size, sniper rate, round-trip rate, median hold time.

round_trip_rate.description: 0–1: fraction of tokens with both buys and sells.

median_hold_minutes.description: Median minutes between first buy and first sell across tokens.

deployer_breakdown.description: Tier distribution of pump.fun deployers this wallet has bought from. Useful for spotting alpha-buyers vs random degens.

tier.description: elite / good / rising / moderate / cold / unranked

recent_trades.description: Last 10 trades regardless of window (raw timeline, cross-joined with deployer-tokens for symbol).

derived.description: Derived wallet stats computed from the enrichments above (src/lib/wallet-enrichments.ts DerivedStats: standout trades, biggest miss, realized/unrealized PnL rollups).

stats_unavailable.description: Present (true) only when the 90-day trade aggregation failed. `stats` null is then UNPROVEN, not an inactive wallet.

enrichment_unavailable.description: Present (true) only when one or more enrichment queries failed; `degraded_fields` names them. Absent on a fully measured response.

degraded_fields.description: Enrichment blocks whose query failed (e.g. a database timeout under load). Their null / [] value is UNKNOWN, not 'no data'; retry later. `biggest_miss` refers to `derived.biggest_miss`. Present only together with `enrichment_unavailable: true`.

WalletHolding.description: One chain-verified token holding. `transfer_delta` = on-chain amount minus trade-derived net (non-null only when the mint was traded in-window); a large positive delta flags tokens received without a swap.

amount_raw.description: Raw integer amount (pre-decimals) as a string.

profit_factor.description: Gross wins / gross losses. null if no losses (undefined math).

pnl_curve.description: Sparse daily UTC buckets — only days with at least one realized event are returned.

closed_positions.description: Tokens where the wallet's position has been fully closed AND there was an observable buy in window. Sorted by pnl_sol DESC (winners first).

cost_basis_observable_from.description: Cost basis can only be reconstructed from trades inside our data window. Overflow sells (no matching buy in window) are silently discarded rather than fabricated.

trades_through.description: Newest trade included — the cache watermark (a later trade invalidates the cached analysis)

trades_through_same_second.description: Trades at exactly trades_through_block_time that were included (block_time is second-granular; used to detect a same-second trade ingested after the compute)

partial.description: Present (true) only when the wallet exceeded the trade analysis cap and the summary was computed from the most recent trades only.

analyzed_trades.description: Present only when partial is true — the number of most-recent trades the summary was computed from (the cap).

get.description: Detects a coordinated launch bundle in a token's earliest-buyer cohort and measures how much of what the bundle bought it still holds. get.summary: Net buy/sell flow by trader cohort on a Robinhood Chain token (PRO+)
get.description:
Splits a token's trade flow into mutually-exclusive trader cohorts over a window, so you can see *who* is accumulating and *who* is distributing.

**Sign convention: `net_eth = sell − buy`.** Positive means the cohort **distributed** (took ETH out); negative means it **accumulated**. Cohorts are assigned by a priority ladder and each trader lands in exactly one: `kol` → `bot` → `dump_cluster` → `early_buyer` → `unprofiled` → `smart_money` → `retail`.

`smart_money` is derived (win-rate ≥ 0.5 and net positive across all tokens), not a stored label. `unprofiled` is a real answer, not a gap — the trader has not met the reputation matview's thresholds. There is deliberately no `fresh_wallet` cohort: Robinhood Chain has no wallet-level first-seen, so it cannot be computed honestly.

get.summary: Peak market cap, drawdown and high-water curve for a Robinhood Chain token (PRO+)

Peak market cap, current drawdown from peak, and a running high-water curve.

**Two peaks are returned, and they can disagree.** `peak_mc_usd_recorded` is the stored high-water mark every other Robinhood Chain surface keys off (deployer runner-rate, the $40K graduation bar). `peak_mc_usd_observed` is the maximum of the 1-minute candle highs — trade-level truth, and always ≥ the recorded value. get.summary: EVM-native risk assessment for a Robinhood Chain token (PRO+)
get.description:
Risk assessment computed **live** against our own Robinhood Chain node at the chain head.

**This is not the Solana risk model.** EVM has no mint or freeze authority. Measured across 300 random Robinhood Chain tokens, only 2.3% even expose an `owner()` function and 0% expose `mint` in their own bytecode — so an absent flag is the norm, not a safety signal. The axes that actually discriminate here are proxy upgradeability, LP custody, and sellability.

**Sellability is the strongest signal.** A sell is simulated through the router at head using state overrides, which detects a token that can be bought but not sold. It is computed live, never cached — whether a token is sellable can change the moment an owner flips a setting.

Proxies are resolved before capability scanning: EIP-1167 minimal proxies (14% of tokens) carry zero selectors of their own, and the tokenized equities are beacon proxies whose *implementation* is what exposes `mint`/`pause`/`upgradeTo`. `lp_custody` is only read for uniswap-v2 pools; v3/v4 liquidity sits in an LP NFT whose custody needs a position-manager trace, and is reported `unknown` rather than guessed.

get.summary: First buyers of a Robinhood Chain token, and whether they still hold (PRO+)
get.description:
The first buyers of a Robinhood Chain token, in order, joined to what happened next. `rhc_early_buyers` ranks the first 20 buyers of 437k tokens and is recomputed daily; until now it was read only as a per-wallet COUNT, never exposed as a per-token list. The Solana counterpart is `GET /kol/tokens/{mint}/entry-order`.

**`realized_eth` is a profit only when `position` is `closed`.** It is `sold_eth - bought_eth`, so a buyer who is still holding shows a negative figure - they have spent and not yet sold. Always read `position` alongside it.

**`still_holding` comes from the ERC-20 Transfer-log fold**, the same source as `/rhc/tokens/{address}/holders`. Treat it as exact only when `holdings_verified` is true.

**Ranks are as of `computed_at`, not live.** A token that began trading after the last sweep returns an empty list with a stated reason - never an assertion that it had no early buyers. Wallets may be ERC-4337 smart accounts, so a wallet is an address, not a person.

get.summary: Holder set and concentration for a Robinhood Chain token (PRO+)
get.description:
Holder balances and concentration metrics. **Not trade-derived** — balances are folded from ERC-20 `Transfer` logs, which our node retains in full, so they are exact rather than estimated. The Solana counterpart is `GET /tokens/{mint}/holders` — a live on-chain census via mint-scoped getProgramAccounts (shipped 2026-08-16).

**Every token carries a reconciliation.** `verified` is true only when the reconstructed `sum(balance)` equals on-chain `totalSupply()` at a pinned block. A token that fails, or has not been swept yet, returns `verified: false` with a stated `unverified_reason` — never as though it were exact.

**Concentration excludes pools and burn addresses.** The largest holder of a token is normally its own liquidity pool, so counting it would make `top1_share` meaningless; pools and burns are reported separately as `pool_held_pct` / `burned_pct` and excluded from the circulating denominator. Balances are raw uint256 and are returned as **strings** to preserve precision. Holder addresses may be ERC-4337 smart accounts, so `holder_count` is not a headcount of people.

**Holder growth (2026-08-17).** `holder_growth.{1h,24h,7d}` reports `entered` (first Transfer at-or-after the window's `cutoff_block`), `entered_still_holding`, `exited` (pre-existing holders whose last movement in the window left them at zero) and `net` ≈ Δ holder_count — possible because the fold keeps first_seen_block/last_block and retains zero-balance rows. The Solana census has no history and cannot answer this.

get.summary: Deployer signal alert feed on Robinhood Chain (BASIC+)
get.description:
The deployer alert feed on Robinhood Chain (from `rhc_deployer_alerts`) — new deploys and graduations from tracked deployers, newest first. RHC domain values differ from Solana: `tier` is elite | good | neutral | spammer, `priority` is high | medium, `alert_type` is new_deploy | graduated (RHC has no bonded/kol_buy alert types, and no KOL-buy enrichment).

**Two behaviours changed 2026-07-25.** (1) A tradability filter is now applied **BY DEFAULT** (`liquidity_usd >= $100`; unknown liquidity fails it) — the feed was serving alerts on tokens that had pumped and drained, one at $45K MC against $68 of liquidity. Pass `include_untradeable=true` for the raw tape; the active filter is echoed as `tradability_filter`. (2) `tier` and the `message` explaining it are now resolved at **READ time** from the live deployer rollup instead of being frozen at insert, so a demoted deployer can no longer be advertised as good-tier indefinitely. The original snapshot is preserved as `tier_at_alert`, with `tier_is_stale` flagging disagreement. Rows also carry `liquidity_usd` and `current_mc_usd`.

**Paging (2026-09-21, audit F09 follow-up):** the tradability and tier gates are served by a bounded SCAN over (event_at DESC, id DESC) — `has_more` is false only at the real end, `scan.scan_truncated` says the budget ran out first; page with `cursor=` (`next_cursor`). Alerts with a NULL event_at (none in production) are excluded.

Tier: **BASIC** (any valid key) — **ULTRA** gets the full requested `limit`, while BASIC/PRO share a 50-alert cap per request.

get.summary: Smart-money wallet ranking on Robinhood Chain (PRO+)
get.description:
Robinhood Chain trader wallets ranked by realized on-chain performance — the reverse of KOL discovery: instead of tracing Solana wallets onto RHC, we rank the wallets we already watch trade. `net_eth` is realized net flow (sell − buy, honest about ignoring unrealized holdings); `win_rate` is the share of traded tokens taken out profitably; `likely_bot` flags atomic-arb/MM fleets (near-perfect win rate across many tokens). Because RHC is dual-natured (launchpad memecoins vs tokenized stocks/stables), `memecoin_share` = launchpad-token trade share — filter with `min_memecoin_share` to isolate memecoin traders, or `max_avg_mc_usd` for low-caps. Derived from our self-hosted node, refreshed every 15 min.

**Zero-cost-basis dumps, filtered by default** (*added 2026-08-29*): `net_eth` is `sell_eth − buy_eth` per wallet, and for a token a wallet never bought (its own on-chain buy leg unattributed — almost always a deployer/insider allocation sold with no purchase), the whole sale counts as "profit" even though it isn't trading skill. `zero_cost_share` is the fraction of a wallet's gross ETH extracted (sell-side) that came from such tokens; wallets at or above 0.5 are excluded from this listing by default (~23% of tracked wallets, concentrated at the very top of a raw net_eth sort) since their ranking and win_rate are inflated by dumps, not performance. The row still exists in the underlying dataset — pass `include_zero_cost_dumps=true` for the unfiltered ranking, and read `zero_cost_share` on each row either way; do not treat a high `net_eth` from this endpoint as trading profit without checking it. Tier: **PRO+**.

get.description:
Any Robinhood Chain wallet's 90-day trading profile: FIFO cost-basis PnL, per-token breakdown, recent trades, and a reputation block (tracked KOL, known deployer + tier, alpha-ranked, dump-cluster membership, early-buyer count).

**Denomination is ETH**, matching the rest of the RHC tree (`eth_amount`, `net_eth`) — not USD. A USD cost basis would silently mix in the tokenized-stock quote assets some flap bonding curves price in.

**Sourced from `trader_eoa` — the effective trading account, never the swap-log `trader`**, which is the router address on any aggregated swap.

`stats.analyzed_trades + stats.unattributed_trades + stats.unsized_trades === stats.total_trades` always holds — no trade silently vanishes from the accounting. The two exclusions mean different things: **`unattributed_trades`** is swaps with no token side at all (token↔token exotic pools, unclassified pools) and is routine, often large for MM bots; **`unsized_trades`** is a token-side trade whose quantity could not be reconstructed from `rhc_trades`' raw uint256 leg amounts, which is the actual quality signal and should be ~0.

**Attribution floor:** analysis starts at `notes.attribution_complete_from` (2026-07-18) rather than the full 90 days — `trader_eoa` was written for under half of earlier trades, and a partial view produces positions the wallet no longer holds.

A wallet exceeding the 50,000-trade analysis cap returns `stats.partial: true`. Heavy wallets that blow the query budget return the reputation block with `stats_unavailable: true` rather than a 500. Responses are cached 60s per address. Tier: **PRO+**.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: EVM wallet address (0x, 40 hex). Case-insensitive; echoed lowercase.

200.description: OK. `stats` is null only when the wallet is known solely through a reputation table (e.g. a deployer that has never traded).

analyzed_trades.description: Trades that entered the FIFO computation.

unattributed_trades.description: Swaps with no token side or direction — token↔token exotic pools and pools our resolver has not classified. Routine, and a large share for MM bots (47% on one 512k-trade fleet wallet). NOT a data-quality signal.

unsized_trades.description: Token-side trades whose QUANTITY could not be reconstructed — excluded from PnL entirely. This IS the quality signal and should be ~0 (measured 0 across a 512k-trade wallet).

unrealized_pnl_eth.description: Mark-to-market on FIFO-open positions using rhc_token_prices.last_price_native. Unpriced positions contribute 0. **FIFO figure, not a holding**: it includes lots transferred out since the buy. For PnL on what is actually held use `holdings.unrealized_known_eth`.

held_value_eth.description: FIFO-unmatched DEX buys x current price. **Not an on-chain balance**: a token sent out by transfer still counts here. The proven current value is `holdings.verified_value_eth`.

open_positions.description: FIFO-open positions (unmatched DEX buys). How many are actually still held is in `holdings`.

partial.description: Present only when the 50,000-trade cap was hit.

is_dumper.description: ≥5 dump cohorts AND 0 runner cohorts, rolling 42d. Rebuilt daily — up to ~48h stale. Absence means NOT OBSERVED, not verified clean.

early_buyer_tokens.description: Tokens where this wallet was in the first-20 buyer cohort.

still_holding.description: FIFO meaning: an unmatched DEX buy exists. NOT an on-chain balance; see holding_status.

holding_status.description: On-chain status of a FIFO-open token; null when the token is FIFO-closed.

holdings.description: On-chain verification of every FIFO-open position: balanceOf + decimals read from our own Robinhood Chain node in one Multicall3 batch (cached 30 s). `complete: false` means at least one position is BALANCE_UNVERIFIED (node unreachable, call reverted, non-standard token, decimals mismatch) and contributes NO value.

verified_value_eth.description: PROVEN balances x current price: the current value of the tokens this wallet bought on a DEX and still holds. Unverified and unpriced positions contribute nothing.

cost_basis_held_eth.description: Cost basis of the FIFO-known portion still in the wallet.

unrealized_known_eth.description: Unrealized PnL on the portion whose cost basis is known AND still held. External inflows never add trading profit.

get.summary: FIFO cost-basis PnL on Robinhood Chain (PRO+)
get.description:
Full FIFO cost-basis PnL for one RHC wallet over 90 days: realized and unrealized split, a daily realized curve, every closed position with ROI and token-weighted hold time, and every open position marked to the current price.

This runs the **same FIFO implementation as the Solana `/wallet/{address}/pnl`** — the algorithm is imported, not reimplemented — with ETH substituted for SOL. Field names keep the Solana convention with the denomination swapped (`realized_eth`, `pnl_eth`), so porting a Solana integration is a mechanical rename.

It also shares its loader with `/rhc/wallet/{address}`, so the two endpoints cannot report different PnL for the same wallet.

**Cost basis is only observable inside the window** (`notes.cost_basis_observable_from`). Tokens sold that were bought before it contribute no realized PnL rather than a fabricated one — figures read low, never invented.

**Attribution floor (`notes.attribution_complete_from`, 2026-07-18):** the window is clamped forward to this date because `trader_eoa` — the column every wallet endpoint filters on — was written for under half of earlier trades. The gap is ASYMMETRIC per wallet: a token's buys can carry it while its sell does not, which leaves FIFO holding a position that was actually closed. Analysing only the attributed era is narrower but honest. `notes.window_clamped` flags it. Cached 120s per address. Tier: **PRO+**.

profit_factor.description: Gross wins / gross losses. null when there are no losses (undefined math), 0 when there are no wins.

pnl_curve.description: Sparse daily UTC buckets of REALIZED PnL. `cumulative_pnl` is the running sum of `day_pnl`; days with no realized events are omitted.

hold_minutes.description: Token-weighted across matched FIFO lots — correct for re-entered tokens.

open_positions.description: Unsold FIFO tail marked to the current price. Each entry carries `liquidity_basis` (`v4_virtual_ceiling` | `measured`) — uniswap-v4 liquidity_usd is a virtual-reserve ceiling, not measured per-pool TVL.

data_through.description: Newest trade this answer was computed from — the response's vintage. Equals `stats.last_seen` on /rhc/wallet/{address} when both ran over the same data. Use this, not a trade count, to tell whether two responses are comparable: the count saturates at the analysis cap.

get.description:
Only what the wallet is still holding, marked to the current price — the same FIFO pass as `/pnl` without the curve and closed-position payload, for clients polling "what is this wallet in right now".

**"Open" means FIFO-unmatched buys inside the window: a TRADING position, NOT an on-chain balance.** This cuts both ways and the second direction is the dangerous one: a token acquired by transfer or bridge does not appear, and a token **disposed of by plain ERC-20 transfer rather than sold on a DEX still appears as held**, because only swaps are indexed. Since 2026-10-02 every position is **checked against the chain**: `current_onchain_balance` (balanceOf from our own node, Multicall3, cached 30 s) sits next to `fifo_unmatched_amount`, and `holding_status` says which applies: `HELD` (balance within 0.5 % of FIFO), `PARTIALLY_REDUCED` (0 < balance < FIFO), `TRANSFERRED_OR_DISPOSED` (balance 0), `EXTERNAL_INFLOW` (balance > FIFO; the excess has no cost basis), `BALANCE_UNVERIFIED` (read failed, non-standard token, or our decimals differ from on-chain decimals: fail closed, no value). The pre-existing fields (`token_amount`, `current_value_eth`, `unrealized_eth`, the `summary` totals) keep their FIFO meaning; `summary.holdings` and the `current_holding_value_eth` / `unrealized_known_eth` fields are the proven-holdings view.

**Attribution floor:** analysis starts at `notes.attribution_complete_from` (2026-07-18), not the full 90 days — `trader_eoa` was written for under half of earlier trades, and a partial view yields positions the wallet no longer holds. `notes.window_clamped` flags when this is what bounds the result. `total_unrealized_eth` is computed against the cost basis of the PRICED subset only — `unpriced_positions` counts what is missing from the totals, so a zero is never mistaken for worthless. Tier: **PRO+**.

200.description: OK. Sorted by current value, then cost basis.

total_unrealized_eth.description: Against the cost basis of the priced subset only.

holdings.description: On-chain verification of every FIFO-open position: balanceOf + decimals read from our own Robinhood Chain node in one Multicall3 batch (cached 30 s). `complete: false` means at least one position is BALANCE_UNVERIFIED (node unreachable, call reverted, non-standard token, decimals mismatch) and contributes NO value.

verified_value_eth.description: PROVEN balances x current price: the current value of the tokens this wallet bought on a DEX and still holds. Unverified and unpriced positions contribute nothing.

cost_basis_held_eth.description: Cost basis of the FIFO-known portion still in the wallet.

unrealized_known_eth.description: Unrealized PnL on the portion whose cost basis is known AND still held. External inflows never add trading profit.

cost_basis_not_held_eth.description: Cost basis of FIFO lots no longer in the wallet (transferred out or disposed outside indexed swaps). Outcome unknown: neither realized nor unrealized.

liquidity_basis.description: How liquidity_usd was derived. uniswap-v4 figures are virtual reserves clamped to the PoolManager's total holdings — a provable ceiling, not measured per-pool TVL.

realized_so_far_eth.description: Partial exits already taken on this token.

fifo_unmatched_amount.description: DEX buys not matched by a DEX sell (same as token_amount). A trading position, not a balance.

current_onchain_balance.description: balanceOf(wallet) / 10^decimals from our node. null = not proven (BALANCE_UNVERIFIED).

held_known_amount.description: min(balance, FIFO): the held part whose cost basis is known.

current_holding_value_eth.description: current_onchain_balance x current price. 0 when transferred out; null when unverified or unpriced.

unrealized_known_eth.description: Unrealized on the known-cost, still-held portion only.

cost_basis_not_held_eth.description: Cost basis of the FIFO portion no longer in the wallet. Outcome unknown.

A deployer whose attributed total dwarfs its collected total is redirecting fees (launch tool, KOL, social handle) — that gap is the signal. get.description: One newest-first timeline of what a deployer wallet did, from data MadeOnSol already holds. **The window applies to each event's own time** (`window.applies_to: event_time`): a sell yesterday of a token launched months ago is inside a 30-day window. Event types: `launch` (every launchpad we index; `fee_payer_is_creator` / `external_fee_payer` say whether the creator paid the create fee, null when unknown; `dev_buy_sol` / `dev_buy_tokens` / `dev_buy_supply_pct` from the create transaction when recorded), `dev_buy` / `dev_sell` (one event per stored trade of the deployer in a token MadeOnSol attributes to it, with `sol`, `tokens`, `price_usd`, `tx`; subject to the trade persistence floor of 0.05 SOL / $3.50; other swaps are on GET /wallet/{address}/trades), `creator_transferred` (pump.fun creator rights moved to or from this wallet: the raw `from` / `to` of the event, `direction`, `initiated_by` creator | platform_admin | other_signer | unknown), `fee_claim` (creator-fee claims paid to the wallet), `funding_in` (one event per funder, timed by the latest transfer, `first_at` = first transfer; recorded only while the wallet is in the funding tracked set) and `capital_out` (one event per recipient address, timed by the latest transfer; recorded only when the wallet is a tracked high-signal source). Addresses in events are raw facts of the concrete event, not identity claims. Every event carries `time_basis` (chain | ingest | chain_or_ingest). `coverage.families.<family>` states each source, retention, scope, `truncated`, `complete`, `complete_from` and `archive_required_before`. **History is served from the online (Postgres) store; older trade months live only in the Parquet archive.** Archive reads for `dev_trades` are being rolled out for ULTRA and BUSINESS (PRO's 30-day window never reaches the archive). While they are off, a window that crosses that boundary is never reported as complete: `dev_trades` answers `complete: false`, `complete_from` = the earliest instant the online store covers completely, `archive_required_before` = the instant before which events exist only in the archive, and `coverage.status` is `partial`. If the boundary cannot be read, the family is `complete: false` with `boundary_known: false`. Fixed-retention families also carry `retention_boundary`: when the dev-event source is enabled, `dev_transfers` (SPL transfers of the deployer's own token) is held 30 days online, so a window starting before `retention_boundary` answers `complete: false` with `complete_from` = `retention_boundary` and `coverage.status: partial` (those rows are pruned, not archived). A wallet MadeOnSol has never attributed a launch to cannot have dev trades: `dev_trades` is then not queried and says `skipped_reason: no_attributed_launch`. `plan.history` separates the requested window (`requested`, `effective` after the tier clamp), the online coverage (`online`, served) and the archive-only range (`archive_only`, null when the window does not reach it). Without archive reads `archive_only` says `served: false`, `reason: archive_reads_not_enabled`. With archive reads, `coverage.families.dev_trades.archive` reports the read (`read` ok | not_needed | failed, `served`, `reason`, `missing_months`, `months_read`) and `archive_only.served` is true only when the archive answered for the whole range; `dev_trades` is then `complete: true` with `archive_required_before: null`. When an archive month is missing, `complete_from` / `archive_required_before` move to the end of the newest missing month (`reason: archive_months_missing`). If the archive is unavailable or times out, the online part is returned with `complete: false` and `reason` archive_unavailable | archive_timeout | archive_contract_mismatch | archive_ledger_unavailable, never an error and never a false complete. **An empty family is not evidence that nothing happened.** Paginate with `cursor` (opaque, ordered by (at, id), never skips equal timestamps). Server-side hard caps by plan (`plan` echoes them): PRO a 30-day window / 100 per page, ULTRA a 365-day window / 100 per page, BUSINESS an unbounded window / 500 per page; a larger `limit` is clamped (`pagination.limit_capped`) and an earlier `since` is clamped to the plan window. The ULTRA and BUSINESS windows normally reach past the online trade boundary, so their `dev_trades` coverage is usually partial (see above). ULTRA and BUSINESS responses carry an `identity` block, which currently answers `status: not_available` (identity stitching is not released; no linked wallets are reported, which says nothing about whether the wallet operates alone). PRO responses never carry an identity block or a fee-payer address. Feature-flagged: answers 503 `feature_disabled` until enabled. PRO+.

get.description:
Browse tokens by market-cap band, liquidity floor, recent-activity window, primary DEX, authority/safety flags, computed 1h volume, MEV-share ceiling, and MC change. Momentum sorts surface movers (`mc_change_5m_desc`, `mc_change_1h_desc`, `volume_1h_desc`) and a composite `trending` board. Complements `/token/{mint}` (single lookup), `/tokens/almost-bonded` (pre-bond pump.fun), and the KOL-scoped `/kol/tokens/{hot,trending}`.

**Default `min_liq` is 2000 USD** to filter the long tail of phantom-MC tokens from low-liquidity pools. Pass `min_liq=0` to opt out.

**Default `max_mc` is 100,000,000,000 USD ($100B)** — a sanity ceiling that drops phantom market caps (a genuine ~1e12 token supply trading near $1, or a thin-pool price blow-up). No real tracked memecoin approaches it. Pass a higher explicit `max_mc` to opt out.

**Momentum sorts + filters are DB-native** (via the `token_prices_trending` view): `min_volume_1h_usd`, `max_mev_share_pct`, `min_liq_mc_ratio`, `max_liq_mc_ratio`, `mc_change_1h_min_pct`, `mc_change_1h_max_pct` and the momentum sorts paginate correctly with no over-fetch. The `trending` sort = recent-volume × positive-momentum composite, recency-bounded to the last 1h, and echoes `filters.trending_version: "v1"`.

**Only `deployer_tier` and `launchpad`** remain post-filters (joined from `deployer_tokens`, not the view). They are served by a bounded SCAN: candidates are walked in pages until `limit` matches, the candidates run out, or the scan budget is spent. `has_more:false` only when the candidates ran out; `pagination.scan_truncated:true` = the budget ran out first and more matches MAY exist — continue with `offset = pagination.next_offset` (a RAW candidate offset, not a match count). Offset pages walk a LIVE order (`pagination.order_is_live: true`): MC and activity move between calls, so rows can shift across pages — treat the screener as a ranking, not a ledger.

**LP burn (2026-09-21):** `lp_burned` / `lp_burn_status` come from LP-custody evidence only (`lp_burnt_pct`). No Solana writer populates it yet, so `lp_burn_status` is `unknown` and `lp_burned` null for every token, and `lp_burned=true|false` currently matches nothing. `lp_burned` is DEPRECATED: `true` = verified burned/locked, `false` = verified NOT burned, and a token with unknown LP custody matches neither (false never turns unknown into "unburned"); a request that sends it gets a `deprecations` entry. The old `lp_burned` flag was the token-SUPPLY burn — filter that with `supply_burn` and read it as `token_supply_burn_detected`.

get.description:
Every captured trade for one token, newest first — the backfill complement to the live firehose (seed history, then keep current via the stream). Per trade: tx_signature, wallet_address, action, sol_amount, token_amount, price_sol/price_usd, market_price_sol/market_price_usd, early_buyer_rank, slot, block_time.

**Two different prices, on purpose.** `price_sol` is *this trade's executed price* — `sol_amount / token_amount`, so it reconciles exactly with the amounts on the same row and with the PnL endpoints. `sol_amount` is the wallet's net SOL movement, so that price is the trader's all-in effective rate: it includes the swap fee and any account rent paid in the same transaction, and it is not the pool mid. `market_price_sol` is our market-cap tracker's canonical pool price sampled near that trade's slot — one value per token per update, so every trade in the same slot shares it. Use `price_sol` for cost basis, fills and PnL; use `market_price_sol` when you want a per-token price series independent of trade size and direction.

*Changed 2026-08-16*: `price_sol`/`price_usd` previously carried the canonical value, which disagreed with the row's own amounts by a 7.9% median (and far more on fast-moving mints, where one slot can span a 60% price swing). The canonical number did not disappear — it moved to `market_price_*`.

**Coverage honesty**: capture starts 2026-04-12 and is pump.fun-pipeline scoped — the `coverage` response object carries both markers. **Size floor**: Buys under 0.05 SOL (under $3.50 when paid in USDC/USDT) are not stored; sells that receive SOL are kept at any size. (`coverage.size_floor`). Default window is full history. PRO+.

**Where the rows come from** (*added 2026-08-29*): closed months older than the newest three move from Postgres to a Parquet archive; pages are split at `history.postgres_from` (Unix seconds) — rows at/after it are served from Postgres, older rows from the archive reader — with the same ordering and cursor. `history.archive_used` says whether this page touched the archive (`archive_months` lists which), `history.archive_available` whether the archive could be reached (`null` = not configured), and `history.truncated: true` means older history was requested but the archive did not answer — retry later rather than treating `has_more:false` as the end of the tape. Response header `X-Read-Source`: `core`, `core+archive` or `archive`.

Same per-mint shape as `GET /tokens/{mint}/buyer-quality`. Shares the LRU cache with the single-mint endpoint — already-warm mints return at ~zero cost. Response includes `cache_hits` counter.

**Coverage** (additive): each item carries `in_scope` (boolean|null) derived from whether that mint had early-buyer rows in our capture — `false` may simply mean 'no early-buyer rows', not proof the token never traded (the batch path does not run the per-mint probe; use the single-mint endpoint for a probed verdict). A top-level `coverage` object carries the shared `history_start` + `scope` markers once.

PRO returns the top 10, ULTRA the full 20 (mv_early_buyer_pnl excludes rank-1, the deployer's own buy). Cohort scope: first 20 buyers (deployer excluded) of launches our deployer pipeline recorded at creation and tracked from that launch; mints admitted later (bags/LaunchLab persist-set, revived curves, restart-loaded history) have no early-buyer cohort, and buyers during an ingest gap are missing.

first_sell_at.description: When this early buyer first sold; null if never sold.

still_holding.description: True if the wallet has not sold (first_sell_at is null).

historical_win_rate.description: Wallet's all-time win rate (0–1), from mv_alpha_wallets.

buyer_quality_score.description: 0–100 composite quality of the early-buyer cohort.

confidence.description: Confidence in the PREDICTIVE inputs: counts only buyers whose win rate fed the score (≥3 tokens of history, not bot-flagged, not zero-cost-dump dominated). insufficient_data = none did — the score is the neutral-50 default plus penalties. 1 → low, 5+ → medium, 11+ → high.

still_holding.description: Cohort members with no confirmed sell on a tracked venue (swap-ledger scoped — a plain transfer out still reads as holding).

get.description: A live holder census read from the ledger at `confirmed`: every token account of the mint (owner + balance via mint-scoped `getProgramAccounts`), merged per owner. Gives an EXACT `holder_count` (distinct non-zero owners minus excluded pools/curves/burns), `token_accounts_nonzero`, ranks 1–100 retained, and `top1/top10/top20/top50/top100_share` over the circulating denominator. Each disclosed owner is labelled from MadeOnSol wallet intelligence (deployer / kol / early_buyer / bundle / bot / dump_cluster). Program-derived owners (liquidity pools, bonding curves, vaults) and burn addresses are EXCLUDED from the denominator and listed in `excluded[]` — the #1 raw account of a fresh memecoin is its own bonding curve. Disclosure: PRO ranks 1–10, ULTRA 1–50, BUSINESS 1–100; the maths is tier-independent. Measured latency: fresh pump.fun mints <1 s, $0.1–2M memecoins ~0.1–1.2 s, 200k–550k-account tokens 6–11 s (503 `holder_scan_in_progress` then cached). Mega-caps the provider refuses (TRUMP/JUP/BONK class) fall back to the top-20 `getTokenLargestAccounts` view with `holder_count: null` and `source.census_fallback_reason` set — never a trade-derived estimate. The same fallback applies when the census times out, and (since 2026-10-02) when a census's balances add up to more than the mint's supply: such a read is not one consistent ledger snapshot, so it is refused rather than served (`census_fallback_reason: census_inconsistent_sum_exceeds_supply`). Distinct from `/cap-table` (who bought first) — this is who holds NOW.

burned_pct.description: Share of total supply at burn addresses.

Each trader is enriched with our reputation data (is_kol, is_alpha_tracked + bot_confidence + historical win rate) so you can separate smart money from a bot round-trip. get.description:
Transparent 0–100 rug-risk score (higher = riskier) with a per-factor breakdown — mint/freeze authority, liquidity depth & thinness, Token-2022 transfer fee, LP burn, bundled/sniped open, deployer track record, KOL distribution, supply inflation (on-chain supply grown above expected = stealth-mint/dilution), and blacklist. Composed from the same data layer as `GET /token/{mint}` (no extra latency). Returns `band` (safe/caution/danger), `factors[]` (each with `status` + `points` + `detail`), and the raw `inputs` (including `supply_inflation_pct` and `sniper_footprint`). The top-level `dev` block (nullable) is the deployer self-activity read: create-tx self-buy (`buy_sol`/`buy_tokens`/`buy_supply_pct`), post-create own-mint trading (`bought_tokens_after`, `sold_tokens`, `sold_sol`, `first_sell_at`/`last_sell_at`), and live on-chain holdings (`holdings_tokens`, `holdings_supply_pct`, `wallet_empty`), each with its own observation time (`holdings_observed_at`, `activity_rollup_through`), plus `transfer_status` (`none_detected` | `suspected` | `unknown`): a balance below what the dev's own recorded trades explain is only ever SUSPECTED (a sell on an uncaptured venue looks identical), and misaligned or missing observations are `unknown`; `transferred_out` is its deprecated boolean view. Carries `score_version` (now `v2`) and `as_of` (response time — not an observation time).

**Score v2 (2026-09-21):** the LP factor no longer credits a token-SUPPLY burn (mc-tracker's burn flag) — LP custody is not observed for Solana pools, so `lp_burn` is warn/8 with `inputs.lp_burn_status: unknown` unless verified LP evidence exists; an unknown transfer fee is warn/4, not "No transfer fee"; deployer reputation scores only an established history. `assessment` says whether every input was observed: `incomplete` lists `unknown_inputs` and the band is never `safe`; a failed lookup of a score-critical input is a retryable 503 (`code: risk_inputs_unavailable`), never a score computed without it. **Same loader on every transport:** `POST /tokens/batch/risk` and x402 return identical scores for identical evidence; batch skips only the live dev-holdings RPC (`dev.holdings_*` null, `transfer_status: unknown`). The `coverage` object (shared TradeCoverage shape) discloses whether the mint sits inside the launchpad trade capture, with a note naming which sub-fields are trade-derived (cohort/sniper/bundle factors, dev sell rollup) vs pure on-chain reads (authorities, liquidity, live holdings) that are unaffected. PRO+.

source.description: How the pool was resolved: from our pool index, or decoded live on-chain (PumpSwap).

mint.description: The mint scored. Equals the path value unless the path was a PumpSwap pool address, in which case this is the pool's resolved mint and `resolved_from` is set.

band.description: Never `safe` while assessment.status is `incomplete`, or with an un-revoked mint/freeze authority

score_version.description: v2 (2026-09-21): a token-supply burn no longer earns the LP-burn credit (v1: burn_detected=true → 0, every other token → 8; v2: every token without verified LP evidence → 8, burned or not — no burn penalty); unknown transfer fee is warn(4) not "No transfer fee"; deployer reputation scores only an established history; unknown inputs keep the band off `safe`.

status.description: ok/warn/danger = evidence read and scored. unknown = the input should exist but could not be read or is insufficient (0 points; listed in assessment.unknown_inputs; band never safe). not_assessed = no evidence source applies to this token (0 points; listed in assessment.not_assessed). Neither is ever positive evidence.

inputs.description: Every scorer input. Enrichment fields are null when unobserved — unknown, not false/0.

token_supply_burn_detected.description: The mint's supply decreased (token burn). Not LP evidence.

lp_burn_status.description: LP burn/lock evidence: `verified` only with measured LP-token custody (lp_burnt_pct ≥ 99). No Solana writer populates LP custody yet, so today every token is `unknown`. A token-supply burn is never promoted to an LP claim.

deployer_history_status.description: null when there is no deployer

deployer_reputation_scored.description: Whether the bonding rate moved the score (established history only)

liquidity_observed_at.description: When the liquidity figure was last observed (mc-tracker last trade). With the creator not assessed, band safe requires this within the last 6 h (null or more than 5 min in the future = not fresh). 6 h is a policy threshold, not proof that the liquidity is still there.

status.description: incomplete = at least one score input is unknown; the score is a lower bound

unknown_inputs.description: Inputs not observed for this token (e.g. transfer_fee, mint_authority, liquidity, kol_activity, deployer_reputation, blacklist, supply_inflation, launch_cohort). deployer_reputation is unknown when a creator lookup failed, when a LAUNCHPAD mint's creator was not recorded (a coverage gap), or when a known creator has no established history.

explanations.description: Why each unknown / not-assessed input is listed, keyed by input name, plus band_cap when the band was capped (creator not assessed and liquidity / liquidity-to-MC not both ok, or the liquidity figure older than 6 h — a policy threshold, not proof of safety). Missing required creator information never yields band safe, for any token.

get.summary: Token momentum fires — new-token surges + dormant-token revivals
get.description: Newest **momentum fires**, newest first. Two kinds: **surge** — a token < 30 min old whose market cap runs hard vs its launch MC (tier 'early' ≤10 min / ≥$12k / ≥3× launch MC; 'strong' ≤30 min / ≥$30k / ≥6× and ≥2× the lowest sample of the last 3 min; 'breakout' ≤2 min / ≥$45k / ≥8×; each tier fires once per mint, and only when SUSTAINED — the level must hold on the current tick and on a sample ≥10 s older, nothing before 20 s of age, so a one-tick same-slot bundle mark is not a surge) — and **revival** — a token with no 1-minute trade candle for ≥24 h that started trading again, CONFIRMED by real buys + buy volume from the tape (≥5 buys, ≥$500 buy volume, ≥1.5× the pre-dormancy MC), never by the price mark alone. Hard gates on both kinds: liquidity ≥ $1.5k and ≥ 2% of MC when known (a thin-pool 'MC' is an artefact), MC ≤ $100B, and the MC gained must be PAID FOR — buy volume on the tape ≥ 3% × (MC − launch / pre-dormancy MC); a price mark moves MC on ~$0 of volume. Every fire carries the burst tape (buys/sells/volume with 'tape.source' = candles | wallet_trades | null — the open minute candle lands only at rollover, so a < 90 s-old surge is measured on the live wallet tape where covered; unique buyers where the mint is in token_trades coverage), tracked-KOL involvement, the first-20 early-buyer cohort (bundled / sold / sniper wallets), deployer reputation and 'risk_flags[]' (bundled_launch, few_buyers, wash_pattern, thin_liquidity, cold_deployer, sniper_heavy, early_buyers_exiting, sell_pressure, no_tape_trades, no_prior_price, mint_authority_active, transfer_fee). Fires ≥65 min old carry 'outcome' (+1 h MC / peak / low) and '?stats=1' prints per-tier hit-rates — out-of-sample by construction. Filters are DB-native: 'kind', 'tier', 'mint', 'launchpad', 'deployer_tier', 'min_mc_usd'/'max_mc_usd', 'min_buys', 'exclude_flags' (comma list), 'only_clean=1'. Cursors 'since'/'before' on fired_at. Pushed live on the **'token:surges'** WebSocket channel and the webhook registry as 'token:surge' / 'token:revival'. The thresholds are echoed in 'definitions' so the docs can never drift from what fires. PRO+.

post.description:
The batch twin of `GET /wallet/{address}/trades`: same rows, same fields, same 90-day window — for **up to 50 wallets per request**, up to 100 trades each, newest first.
