Present the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on the handshake (preferred) or `?token=` — it is masked in our access logs either way. ULTRA and BUSINESS responses also include `dex_ws_url` for the DEX firehose. PRO/ULTRA only.

After connecting, send `{"type":"subscribe","channels":[...]}` — nothing is delivered until you subscribe. Channels: `kol:trades`, `kol:coordination` (PRO+, user-scoped: fires of your own /kol/coordination/alerts rules), `kol:first_touches` (PRO+), `deployer:alerts`, `wallet_tracker:events` (ULTRA, subscriber-scoped), `copytrade:signals` (PRO+, user-scoped), `price_alert:events` (PRO+, user-scoped), `sniper:deploys` (PRO+, tier-curated), `token:graduations` (PRO+ — every pump.fun graduation, tracked deployer or not), `token:prices` (PRO+, **mint-scoped**: `filters.mints` is required and capped per connection at 25 PRO / 100 ULTRA / 250 BUSINESS — a subscribe above the cap is rejected, never truncated; ~250 ms coalesced ticks, event `token:price`), `token:locks` (PRO+ — new Streamflow / Jupiter Lock / Bonfida lock or vesting contracts), `token:fee_claims` (PRO+ — pump.fun creator-fee distributions, social-handle claims and config changes), `token:surges` (PRO+ — token momentum fires: events `token:surge` for new tokens running vs their launch MC, tiers early/strong/breakout, and `token:revival` for ≥24 h-dormant tokens confirmed trading again; subscribe filters `kinds[]`, `tiers[]`, `launchpads[]`, `exclude_flags[]`, `min_mc_usd`/`max_mc_usd`, `deployer_tier[]`), and for **Robinhood Chain** `rhc:kol_trades` (PRO+), `rhc:dex_trades` (ULTRA+), `rhc:dex_trades_unattributed` (ULTRA+ — the additive complement to `rhc:dex_trades`: trades on a pool where no single side could be classified as the token, either because both sides are recognized quote/equity-quote assets like WETH/USDG, or, rarer, because neither is. Fully present in `rhc_trades` but omitted from `rhc:dex_trades`; subscribe to both for full chain coverage. Raw leg data only — `token_in`/`token_out`/`amount_in`/`amount_out`, no decimals/symbol enrichment, no buy/sell `action`), `rhc:new_tokens` (ULTRA+, one event per token the moment its symbol/name/decimals first resolve on chain, before its first trade), `rhc:copytrade:signals` (PRO+, user-scoped), `rhc:price_alert:events` (PRO+, user-scoped), `rhc:kol:coordination` (PRO+, user-scoped), `rhc:kol:first_touches` (PRO+, broadcast — ULTRA is required for the first-touch *subscription* endpoint, not for this channel) , `rhc:token_locks` (PRO+, broadcast: one event per token lock or vesting contract created on chain; withdrawals are not tracked) and `rhc:token_prices` (PRO+, **address-scoped**: `filters.addresses` is required and capped per connection at 25 PRO / 100 ULTRA / 250 BUSINESS (counted across named subscriptions), rejected above the cap, never truncated; event `rhc:token_price`: one snapshot per address on subscribe (`snapshot: true`, from the current price row), then ticks derived from the RHC trade feed at most once per address per 250 ms with the latest value, each carrying `quality` fresh | stale | unreliable and `quality_reason` (no_price, dust_trade, curve_live, state_quote_fallback, low_liquidity, price_age, mc_ceiling), `price_source`, `source_pool`, `liquidity_usd`, `observed_at`, `price_age_ms`; a stale or unreliable price is never delivered as fresh; state stream with no seq/id, a resume gets a fresh snapshot; under a named subscription every frame carries `sub_id`), `rhc:lp_events` (ULTRA+, RHC liquidity events: add / remove / pool_created on tracked Uniswap v2/v3/v4 pools with in_range + share + material; filters addresses, pools, dexes, actions, material_only, min_share), and the Phase 4 scoped channels, all PRO+ and all capped per connection at 25 PRO / 100 ULTRA / 250 BUSINESS tokens or wallets, each channel its own budget, rejected above the cap and never truncated: `token:candles` (**mint-scoped**, `filters.mints` required: live 1-minute candles, the stored row when the minute closes, optional in-progress minute with `filters.updates: true`), `rhc:token_candles` (**address-scoped**, `filters.addresses` required: the same for Robinhood Chain, plus revisions of a rewritten candle), `token:risk` (**mint-scoped**: risk-INPUT changes, mint or freeze authority revoked, transfer fee changed, first supply-inflation crossing; not a risk band or score stream), `rhc:token_risk` (**address-scoped**: a stored RHC risk verdict that changed at a sweep recheck), `wallet:scores` (**wallet-scoped**, `filters.wallets` required: deployer tier changes and KOL categorical state changes) and `rhc:wallet_scores` (**wallet-scoped**, `filters.wallets` with 0x addresses: RHC deployer tier changes). `rhc:dex_trade` / `rhc:dex_trade_unattributed` payloads carry additive enrichment since 2026-09-22: `amount_in_raw` / `amount_out_raw` as exact decimal strings (never floats), `token` + `quote` {address, symbol, decimals} (`token_in_meta` / `token_out_meta` on the unattributed channel), `metadata_status` known | pending | unknown, `price_status` fresh | stale | none with `price_source` and `price_observed_at`, `mc_status` (why `mc_usd` is null), `side` buy | sell only when a canonical quote defines the token, else null with `side_reason`; a KOL trade appears on both `rhc:kol_trades` and `rhc:dex_trades` with the same `tx_hash` + `log_index` and different ids. **30 channels total** (16 Solana + 14 Robinhood Chain; the registry is `services/shared/stream-channels.mjs` and the `connected` frame echoes it). `rhc:trades` is accepted as a deprecated alias of `rhc:dex_trades` (older RHC SDKs sent it) — new code should subscribe to `rhc:dex_trades`. RHC channels ride the SAME socket and the same connection limit as the Solana channels — no second connection needed — but carry EVM-native fields (lowercase `0x` addresses, `eth_amount`, `tx_hash`, `block_number`), so do not reuse a Solana deserializer unchanged.

**Liquidity and lock lifecycle (Phase 3, 2026-09-23).** `rhc:lp_events` delivers event `rhc:lp_event` (id `rhc:lp_event:<tx_hash>:<log_index>`) with `action` add | remove | pool_created, raw `amount0`/`amount1` strings (null on v4, whose ModifyLiquidity reports no token amounts), the position range, `in_range`, `active_liquidity_delta`, `active_share` / `active_share_reason`, `share_of_reserves` (v2) and `material` (a removal of at least 25 % of reserves or active liquidity). `in_range` and the active fields are null (`pool_state_unknown`) when the pool's current tick was not known, never guessed; `provider` is usually a router or position manager, not the beneficial owner; there is no USD field. Invalid lp filters reject the channel rather than widening it. Durable resume from storage (up to 10,000 rows). On `token:locks` and `rhc:token_locks`, `filters.lifecycle: true` opts a subscription into lifecycle events (without it the channel is unchanged): Solana `token:lock_claimed`, `token:lock_cancelled`, `token:lock_closed`, `token:lock_updated` (change topup | extended | schedule_changed | recipient_changed), `token:unlock_upcoming` (next unlock within 24 h) and `token:unlock_available` (the unlock passed within 30 min: claimable per the schedule, NOT claimed); Robinhood Chain `rhc:token_unlock_upcoming` / `rhc:token_unlock_available` only, because RHC claims, extensions and cancels are not observable (`withdrawals_tracked: false`). Further lifecycle filters: `events[]`, `unlock_kinds[]` (cliff, period, final, tranche), `include_automatic_claims` (default false: Streamflow keeper-cranked withdrawals, about 90 % of claim volume, are hidden unless set), and `mints` (Solana) / `addresses` (RHC). Ids are `<event>:<event_key>`, deduplicated durably server-side, and no event is emitted for history (backfills and reconciliation never alert).

**Candles, risk inputs and wallet scores (Phase 4, 2026-09-23).** All six channels are scoped only (no firehose on any tier). The cap counts the union across every named subscription on the connection, and each channel has its OWN budget: one PRO socket may watch 25 price mints, 25 candle mints and 25 risk mints at once. A missing or empty scope, a malformed entry or a scope above the cap rejects the channel (`channels_rejected`; codes `candles_missing_filter`, `candles_invalid_scope`, `candles_over_cap`, `candles_invalid_filters`, `risk_scope_missing`, `risk_scope_invalid`, `risk_scope_over_cap`, `risk_invalid_filters`, `wallet_scores_missing_filter`, `wallet_scores_invalid_filter`, `wallet_scores_over_cap`), an `update` that would make it invalid is refused whole (`invalid_filters`), and a downgrade above the new cap revokes it (`channels_revoked`). The generic filter keys (`action`, `min_mc_usd`, ...) never apply to these events. Their events enter the in-memory replay buffer only while a connected subscription watches the token or wallet, so a resume of a subscription holding them is served from storage; put them in their own named subscription. None of these event types can be registered as a webhook.

**Candles.** Events `candle:closed` (Solana) and `rhc:candle_closed` / `rhc:candle_revised` (RHC) carry the stored 1-minute row (`bucket_start`, `bucket_end`, `closed_at`, open/high/low/close price and MC, liquidity, supply, volumes, `trades`, buy/sell counts, `dex`, `pool_address`, `final: true`, `source`; RHC adds `revision` / `revised_at`). Id `candle:<chain>:<token>:<bucket_start epoch s>`, a revision appends `:r<n>`. With `filters.updates: true` the channel also sends `candle:update` / `rhc:candle_update`: the producer's in-progress minute, at most one per token per second, a state stream with no seq/id that is never replayed (`replay_end.channels.<ch>.updates` says `mode: none`, `gap: state_stream`), and with no snapshot of the open candle on subscribe (the first update comes with the next price move). A fully flat candle with no trades (o = h = l = c, 0 trades) is not emitted live and not replayed. Solana has no revised event: a rare merged rewrite of a minute is published under the same id as the first close. RHC replays only the latest revision of a candle. Frames arrive up to about 25 s after the minute ends. Durable resume from the candle tables for the subscription's tokens only, up to 10,000 rows.

**Risk inputs.** `token:risk` events `risk:authority_changed` (field `mint_authority` | `freeze_authority` | `transfer_fee`, `before` / `after`, `observed_at`, `previous_observed_at`) and `risk:supply_inflated` (level `warn` | `danger` at 0.5 % / 5 %, first crossing per level); `rhc:token_risk` event `rhc:risk_verdict_changed` (`changed`, `before` / `after` verdict, `flags_added` / `flags_removed`, `checked_at`, `previous_checked_at`, `detection`). These are changes of the risk INPUTS, never of the risk band or score, which moves with price and is not streamed (use GET /tokens/{mint}/risk). `slot` is null on the Solana events. The RHC score is higher = safer, the opposite of the Solana `risk_score`. RHC detection lag is NOT bounded to 24 h: the change happened somewhere in (`previous_checked_at`, `checked_at`], currently days to weeks apart (a full recheck cycle takes about 24 days, and only tokens with at least $500 liquidity are rechecked). On subscribe, on an `update` that changes the scope and on a resume, the server sends one state frame per token, `risk:inputs` / `rhc:risk_verdict` with `snapshot: true` and no id or seq; opt out with `filters.risk_snapshot: false`. Optional `filters.risk_events` narrows the event types. Ids `<event>:<event_key>`; durable resume from the event logs.

**Wallet scores.** `wallet:scores` events `deployer:tier_changed` (`tier_before`, `tier_after`, `entered_ranking`, `stats`) and `kol:score_state_changed` (only `is_cold`, `is_heating_up`, `auto_strategy_tag`); `rhc:wallet_scores` event `rhc:deployer_tier_changed`. `filters.wallets` is the scope key on BOTH chains (base58 wallets for Solana, 0x deployers for RHC; not `filters.addresses`, which means token addresses); optional `filters.score_events`. Every frame says when the value was RECOMPUTED, not when it changed: `source` `live_write` (a bond or deploy reclassified the deployer, real time), `scheduled_recompute` (the 6-hourly stats worker, the underlying stats can be hours older) or `matview_refresh` (the 10-minute KOL / 5-minute RHC recompute), with `computed_at` meaning that write, that run or that refresh. A Solana deployer entering a ranked tier from `unranked` counts as a tier change (`tier_before: unranked`, `entered_ranking: true`). No numeric or percentile score stream and no unscoped stream. Ids `<event>:<event_key>`; durable resume from the event logs.

User-scoped channels deliver only your own rule fires; the rest are broadcast.

**Event ids, sequence numbers, resume and replay (Phase 1, 2026-09-22).** Event frames carry `seq` and `id`; `token:price` ticks carry neither. `seq` is ONE ordinal per server process, shared by every channel and every customer and assigned before your filters run, so the seq values you receive have gaps in normal operation: **a gap is not evidence of loss**. `id` is stable: the same event has the same id live, re-sent from memory, rebuilt from storage or recovered after a bus reconnect, so delivery is **at-least-once; dedupe by `id`**. The `connected` frame carries the current `seq`, an `instance` id and the replay window.

**Resume.** Keep a cursor `{instance, seq, ts}` of the last frame your handler finished processing (it returned, or its promise settled) and reconnect with `{type:subscribe, channels, resume:{instance, seq, ts}}`. The `subscribed` ack echoes `resume` with `accepted: true` (`accepted: false`, `reason: replay_in_progress` plus a `warning` frame with that code when a replay is already running on the connection; its channels are still subscribed). Same instance and the cursor still inside the in-memory buffer (last 20,000 frames, about 6-8 minutes): frames are re-sent from memory (`mode: ring`, with their `seq`). Otherwise (server restart = `instance_changed`, or a longer absence = `ring_truncated`) each channel is rebuilt from storage from the cursor's `ts` (minus 60 s slack, deduped by id), bounded to **60 minutes, 2,000 rows per channel and 20,000 rows in total** (`rhc:dex_trades` / `rhc:dex_trades_unattributed`: 10 minutes back and up to 10,000 rows, which can include trades that were never pushed live). Rebuilt frames carry `seq: null`, `mode: durable`, `replayed: true`, and `partial: true` + `missing: [...]` where a field is not stored. `token:graduations` and `rhc:new_tokens` have no stored source: whatever the memory buffer holds is re-sent, then the channel reports gap `not_reconstructable`. `token:prices` gets the current price row per watched mint once (`snapshot: true`, `partial: true`). A resume or legacy replay is ALWAYS bracketed by `replay_start` and `replay_end`, even with nothing to replay. `replay_end` carries `sent`, `matched`, `complete`, `reason`, `retryable`, `retry_after_ms?`, `resume_ts_hint?`, `incomplete_channels?`, `last_seq`, `last_ts` (maxima over frames sent; `last_seq` never above `live_from_seq - 1`), `live_from_seq`, `mode`, `resume_reason`, `count` (legacy, equals `matched`) and `channels: {<channel>: {mode, sent, matched, complete, reason?, gap?, time_basis?, max_rows?, retryable?, retry_after_ms?, late_ingest_possible?, partial?, missing?, approximate?, since_ts?, truncated_at_ts?, gap_before_ts?}}`; reasons are `backpressure`, `instance_changed`, `ring_truncated`, `window_exceeded`, `row_cap`, `source_busy`, `source_error`, `late_ingest_possible`, `not_reconstructable`.

**Commit rule.** Replayed frames do not move your saved cursor (a storage replay is sent channel by channel, not in one time order). On `complete: true`, commit `{instance, seq: last_seq, ts: last_ts}` (keep your previous value where one is null) and let live frames advance it again. On `complete: false, retryable: true`, keep the cursor you resumed from and resume again after `retry_after_ms` (from `ts: resume_ts_hint` ONLY when the reply carries one — the server emits it when every incomplete RETRYABLE channel was cut by `row_cap` (a channel with a FINAL gap, such as `not_reconstructable` on `token:graduations` or `rhc:new_tokens`, does not block the hint, because retrying could not fetch anything behind it); with a mixed retryable set (say one `row_cap` and one `source_error` channel) there is no hint and you resume from your pre-resume cursor, because the hint would step past the failed channel's unread range. Per-channel `truncated_at_ts` is always present for a client that tracks channels separately); duplicates are dropped by id. On `complete: false, retryable: false` the reported gaps are final (`not_reconstructable`, `window_exceeded`, `ring_truncated`, `instance_changed`): backfill them from REST, then commit as for complete. SDK behaviour: on a retryable incomplete recovery our SDKs resume again on the same socket after `retry_after_ms` (up to `maxResumeRetries`, default 5), using `resume_ts_hint` only when every incomplete retryable channel is `row_cap`. The budget is per connection and its counter resets on every (re)connect. When that budget is spent, the gap event says `exhausted: true`: the client stops asking on that connection, the committed cursor stays where it is, and the next reconnect resumes again. On a FINAL gap they emit a gap event first (channels, reason, permanent, the server's bounds and the RANGE that may be incomplete as `skipped.from` -> `skipped.to`) with `advancedPastGap:true` and `source:"auto"`, then move the cursor past it. A count of missing events is never given because it cannot be known. That advance is the client library's own decision, not your approval: set `onUnrecoverableGap:"stop"` to keep the cursor instead, which stops the stream and emits fatal with the same gap, and `acceptGap()` then re-reports it with `source:"manual"` and continues. WATERMARK AND HOLDBACK: a row's id or timestamp is assigned when it is written, not when it commits, so a row with a lower id can still appear after a read passed it. The server therefore advances the committable watermark only across rows whose writing transaction had already finished when the read took its snapshot (xmin_blocked:true when it stops early), holds it 5 s behind now (holdback_ms) and re-scans the last 60 s (rescan_ms) on the next resume; a stuck long transaction cannot freeze it forever (capped at `maxHoldbackMs`, reported as `holdback_capped_ms`). While the cap is in force the channel reports `holdback_ms: 300000` (the nominal 5000 stays as `nominal_holdback_ms`) and its `guarantee` states the real bound and says `CAPPED`: about 6 minutes (5 min + the 60 s re-scan), not the usual 65 s. Frames are still delivered as they are read; the holdback only limits what you may commit, and last_ts is held to the tightest safe_ts (per channel in replay_end.channels.<ch>.watermark {scheme, safe_ts, holdback_ms, nominal_holdback_ms?, holdback_capped_ms?, rescan_ms, xmin_blocked, gate_ms?, guarantee}, overall in replay_end.watermark_safe_ts). RECOVERY IS BOUNDED, NOT A COMPLETENESS GUARANTEE: with the id and ingest-time schemes a write whose transaction commits more than about 65 s after its id or timestamp was taken can be missed (about 6 minutes instead while `holdback_capped_ms` is set), and for rhc:dex_trades / rhc:dex_trades_unattributed (scheme producer_gate) recovery is bounded by the producer's 600 s freshness rule, so a trade already older than 600 s when it was ingested is not recoverable through this path at all. Each channel states its own bound in watermark.guarantee. **Late writes:** every storage read pages by an ingest-time column, a storage id or the producer's own freshness window, so a row written late is not skipped; a channel that could not rule that out would report `complete: false`, `reason: late_ingest_possible`, never `complete: true`. **Load:** recovery is limited server-wide; a resume waits up to 20 s for a slot, otherwise its storage-backed channels report `source_busy` with `retry_after_ms` (memory frames are still sent). A second replay request while one is still running gets only a `replay_in_progress` warning, no second `replay_start` / `replay_end`. Live frames that arrive during a replay are held (up to 5,000 frames or 4 MB per socket, counting each subscription's copy of a frame, so N overlapping named subscriptions use N slots per event; price ticks coalesced per mint and subscription) and delivered after `replay_end`, skipping ids already sent. A socket that cannot drain during a replay gets `complete: false`, `reason: backpressure` and a 4008 close; reconnect and resume. Frames can only be lost across a disconnect or a 4008 close, and the resume reply states what was and was not recovered. **Legacy:** `replay_since_seq` / `replay_since_ts` still work, from memory only; `replay_start` now reports `replay_truncated: true` with `reason` `instance_changed` or `ring_truncated` instead of replaying nothing silently. If the server's own event-bus connection drops, missed events are re-read from storage (up to 60 minutes, 5,000 rows per channel, 10,000 for the RHC DEX trade channels) and delivered with `replayed: true`, `recovered: bus`.

**Entitlements.** Every frame is checked against your current plan; after a downgrade, channels above it are dropped with a `warning` frame `code: channels_revoked` (also a `token:prices` mint set above the new cap). Revoking or rotating your API key deletes the stream token: open sockets close with 4001 within about a minute; mint a new one with the new key. Heartbeat pings every 15 s. Connection slots: PRO 2 · ULTRA 3 · BUSINESS 10 (see /stream/sessions to list or evict a slot).

**Named subscriptions (Phase 2).** A subscribe without `sub_id` is the connection's implicit `default` subscription: one channel set and one filter object for the whole socket (`action: "buy"` on it also drops `deployer:alerts`, whose payload has no action), exactly as before. A subscribe carrying `sub_id` (1-64 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -`) opens or extends an independent subscription with its OWN channels and filters: `{type:subscribe, sub_id, channels, filters}` is acked `subscribed {sub_id, channels, filters, seq, instance, resume?}`, `{type:update, sub_id, filters}` REPLACES that subscription's filters (`updated {sub_id, filters}`), `{type:unsubscribe, sub_id}` removes it (`unsubscribed {sub_id}`; with `channels` it drops only those; a bare `{type:unsubscribe}` still clears every subscription and now acks `unsubscribed {channels: [], all: true}`), and `{type:list}` answers `subscriptions {list:[{sub_id, channels, filters}], count, max}`. Every frame delivered under a named subscription carries `sub_id`; the default subscription's frames carry none. **An event that matches several subscriptions is delivered once per matching subscription**, each copy stamped with its `sub_id`, so dedupe by `(sub_id, id)`. Filters of one subscription never affect another; tier gates, user scoping and revocation apply per subscription (`channels_revoked` names the `sub_id`). Refusals are `warning` frames with the `sub_id` and one of `invalid_sub_id`, `too_many_subscriptions`, `unknown_sub_id`, `invalid_filters`, `channels_rejected`, `replay_in_progress`. The cap counts every subscription on the connection, the default one included: **PRO 5 · ULTRA 10 · BUSINESS 20** (`named_subscriptions.max_per_connection` in this response). `token:prices` mints are capped per CONNECTION across all subscriptions. Resume is per subscription: a subscribe with `sub_id` and `resume` replays only that subscription's channels through its own filters (its `replay_start` / `replay_end` carry the `sub_id`); a client holding several subscriptions re-sends each of them with the SAME cursor on reconnect, the server serves the replays one after another (`resume.queued: true` on the acks that wait; a repeat request for a sub_id that already has one running or queued is refused `replay_in_progress`) and holds live frames until the last `replay_end`; commit the cursor only after the last one, at the smallest `last_seq` / `last_ts` across them. The cursor itself stays per connection (`seq` / `ts` are global).

200.description: OK — { token, ws_url, expires_at: null, next_refresh_at: null, rotated, lifetime, dex_ws_url?, channels[], token_prices: { ... }, named_subscriptions: { ... } }

expires_at.description: Always null — tokens do not expire, kept for wire compatibility

rotated.description: true when this call replaced a previous token (rotate:true was sent, or an existing token was minted fresh)

lifetime.description: Human-readable explanation of the non-expiring token lifecycle

dex_ws_url.description: Present for ULTRA/BUSINESS only — the DEX firehose socket (wss://madeonsol.com/ws/v1/dex-stream). Frames: `dex:trades` (one normalized trade per transaction, the signer's net effect; dedupe by tx_signature), in-band `dex:graduations` on mint-scoped subscriptions, and, since 2026-09-22, the opt-in per-pool view: subscribe with `legs: true` (or `"only"`) to receive per transaction one `dex:route` {signature, slot, signer, hop_count, leg_ids[], shape, decoded_complete, undecoded_program_ids[], liquidity_actions[], router_program, signer_net[], trade_mint} and one `dex:leg` per decoded pool swap {leg_id = `<signature>:<instruction_index>[.<inner_index>]` (stable live and on replay), program, venue, pool_model, pool, pool_kind, pool_authority, vault_in, vault_out, token_in/token_out {mint, amount_raw (integer string), decimals, amount_ui, native}, side, amount_basis, is_route_member}, followed by the unchanged `dex:trades` frame exactly once (omitted with `legs: "only"`). Liquidity deposits/withdrawals are never a leg (listed on the route). The `subscribed` ack of a legs subscription carries `coverage.decodable_programs`; a route touching a program we do not decode says `decoded_complete: false` and names it. **Liquidity events (2026-09-23):** subscribe with `liquidity: true` (in addition to trades) or `"only"` (liquidity frames only; cannot be combined with `legs`) to receive `dex:liquidity` {id = `<signature>:<ix>[.<inner>]`, action pool_created | add | remove, program, venue, instruction, pool, pool_kind, pool_model, mints[{mint, amount_raw, decimals, side in|out}], lp_mint, owner, signer, amount_basis, reserves_before[] / reserves_after[] (raw vault balances), share_of_reserves (constant-product only), depth_effect, material (a removal of at least 25 % of reserves)}. Filters per subscription: token_mint(s), wallet(s), pool(s), dex, program (one of them is required with `"only"`), actions, min_share_of_reserves, material_only. Only liquidity instructions proven by a real transaction fixture are emitted (listed with `emits_events` in the ack's `liquidity_coverage`); other recognised ones appear on the route as `event: false`. Concentrated pools (CLMM, Whirlpool, DLMM) report share and depth as unknown; Meteora DAMM v1, Raydium LaunchLab and Moonshot are not emitted; there is no USD field and `min_usd` is rejected. Replay from the in-memory ring only; no durable resume (`not_reconstructable`). Full protocol in docs/api.md § DEX Firehose.

get.summary: Bulk Parquet exports of archived months (BUSINESS+)
get.description:
BUSINESS+ (BASIC/PRO/ULTRA get 403 with an `upgrade` block; ENTERPRISE passes). Two modes on one route.

**Listing** (no params): every fully archived closed month per dataset — `token_trades`, `rhc_trades`, `token_ohlc_1m`, `rhc_ohlc_1m` — with row count, byte size and file count. A month appears only once both archive providers have verified it (the same ledger the nightly archive exporter writes), so the list is the set you can actually download.

**Download** (`dataset` + `month`): presigned S3 GET links for that month's Parquet files (zstd-compressed, one or more files per month). Links are valid for about **1 hour** — fetch them when you are ready to download, not ahead of time; re-request to mint fresh ones. The ledger row count is returned so you can verify the files you pulled. Both params are required together.

The current (open) month is never listed — it is live in Postgres and served by the paginated endpoints (`/tokens/{mint}/trades`, `/rhc/trades`, `/tokens/{mint}/candles`). Files are identical to the immutable dual-provider archive described at https://madeonsol.com/data-integrity — ideal for backtests, model training and offline analytics without paging through the API.
